findings.what: `NSDictionary *status = TGUserStatusInfo(obj[@"status"]);` is called at line 351 but the function is only defined at line 555 (`static NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(...)`); the same pattern exists for `text = TGMessagePreview(m);` at line 877 vs. its definition at line 1628. Only `TGFlattenMessage` has a forward declaration (line 9). The Makefile builds with `-Wno-implicit-function-declaration` (Makefile:280/285), so this compiles silently.
findings.failure: With no visible prototype clang codegens the call against the implicit signature `int f()`. On the armv7 slice the 32-bit return in r0 happens to alias the pointer, so it works by accident. On the arm64 slice (build/arm64/obj/src/TGClient.o is built by the same Makefile) the return value is truncated to a 32-bit int and sign-extended, so `status` / `text` is a garbage pointer: the very next `status[@"isOnline"]` (line 360) or `text.length` (line 884) messages a wild address and crashes with EXC_BAD_ACCESS on the first updateUserStatus / on every non-text message.
findings.fix: Next to the existing forward declaration at TGClient.m:9 add `static NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(NSDictionary *status);` and `static NSString *TGMessagePreview(NSDictionary *message);`. Do not rely on -Wno-implicit-function-declaration to keep hiding it.

findings.what: `obj[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"][0]` indexes element 0 of a TDLib array with no count check. Same unguarded `[0]` at lines 205 (`updateUser`), 1365 (`contactsWithCompletion:`), 1428 (`userForPhone:`) and 2267 (`ensureUserName:`).
findings.failure: td_api's `usernames` object is `active_usernames:vector<string> disabled_usernames:vector<string> editable_username:string`. A user who owns a username but has it disabled gets a non-nil `usernames` object with an EMPTY `active_usernames` array. `array[0]` then goes through -objectAtIndexedSubscript: and raises NSRangeException, which is uncaught on the main queue. At line 193 this happens on the getMe reply, i.e. the app terminates during login for such an account; at line 205 any `updateUser` for such a contact kills the app mid-session.
findings.fix: Replace every `x[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"][0]` with a guarded helper, e.g. add `static NSString *TGFirstUsername(NSDictionary *u){ NSArray *a = u[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"]; return ([a isKindOfClass:NSArray.class] && a.count && [a[0] isKindOfClass:NSString.class]) ? a[0] : nil; }` and call it at 193, 205, 1365, 1428, 2267.

findings.what: `-forumTopicsForChat:completion:` reads the topic id as `info[@"message_thread_id"]` and pages with `@"offset_message_thread_id" : @(0)` (line 1898). td_api.tl:3911 says `forumTopicInfo chat_id:int53 forum_topic_id:int32 ...` — there is no `message_thread_id` field — and td_api.tl:12510 says `getForumTopics ... offset_forum_topic_id:int32 ...`.
findings.failure: `info[@"message_thread_id"]` is always nil, so every returned topic carries `@"threadId" : @(0)`. Any caller opening a topic with that id would send `message_thread_id: 0` and land in the merged chat stream instead of the topic, and paging would restart from the top forever. The request field `offset_message_thread_id` is also unknown to this TDLib and is ignored.
findings.fix: Either delete this method (see the dead-code finding — TGTopicsViewController.m:781/863 use TGClient+Forums.m's `-forumTopicsForChat:query:offsetDate:offsetMessageId:offsetTopicId:limit:completion:` instead), or change line 1906 to `info[@"forum_topic_id"]` and line 1898 to `@"offset_forum_topic_id" : @(0)`. If deleted, also remove the declaration at TGClient.h:99.

findings.what: `-premiumStateWithCompletion:` gates on `if (![me[@"is_premium"] boolValue]) { completion(nil); return; }`, but `self.me` is constructed at lines 190-195 with exactly four keys: `id`, `first_name`, `username`, `phone`. It never contains `is_premium`. The line below (1481) also reads `state[@"state"][@"expiration_date"]`, while td_api.tl:8166 declares `premiumState state:formattedText ...` — a formattedText has no `expiration_date`.
findings.failure: The completion is unconditionally called with nil for every account, premium or not, so the premium row never appears; even if the guard were removed, the expiry lookup would always miss and the answer would be the bare string "Active".
findings.fix: Add `@"is_premium" : obj[@"is_premium"] ?: @NO` (and `@"last_name"`) to the `self.me` dictionary built at TGClient.m:190, and take the expiry from the account's own `getUserFullInfo` / `premium_expiration_date` option rather than from `premiumState`, which only carries promo text. The same stale `self.me[@"is_premium"]` read exists at TGClient+Premium.m:168.

findings.what: In `-chatProfile:completion:` the shared `answer` block does `@"members" : full[@"member_count"] ?: @0;` and it is used for both supergroups (line 1959) and basic groups (line 1963). td_api.tl:2696 `basicGroupFullInfo photo description creator_user_id members:vector<chatMember> ...` has no `member_count` field.
findings.failure: Opening the profile of a plain (non-super) group shows "0 members" no matter how many members it has, because `full[@"member_count"]` is nil for basicGroupFullInfo.
findings.fix: In the `answer` block use `@"members" : full[@"member_count"] ?: @([full[@"members"] count])`, or pass the count in from each branch: supergroups from `member_count`, basic groups from `[full[@"members"] count]`.

findings.what: `-applyChatUpdate:` handling a single-list `updateChatPosition`: the archive branch does `info[@"archiveOrder"] = ...; info[@"order"] = @(0);` and the main branch (line 2418) does `info[@"archiveOrder"] = @(0);`. One list's position update clobbers the order the chat holds in the other list.
findings.failure: TDLib removes a chat from a list by sending updateChatPosition for that list with order "0". When a chat lives in the archive and TDLib emits the chatListMain removal (order 0), line 2416-2418 sets order=0 AND archiveOrder=0; `-rebuildChats` (2440-2443) then puts the chat in neither `chats` nor `archivedChats`, so an archived chat silently vanishes from the archive until an unrelated full `updateNewChat` re-seeds it.
findings.fix: Only write the field that belongs to the list named in `position[@"list"][@"@type"]`: in the chatListArchive branch set `archiveOrder` only, in the chatListMain branch set `order` and `isPinned` only. Drop both `= @(0)` clobbers at lines 2415 and 2418.

findings.what: `-statusForUser:completion:` decides "today" with `BOOL today = [[NSCalendar currentCalendar] components:NSDayCalendarUnit fromDate:date].day == [[NSCalendar currentCalendar] components:NSDayCalendarUnit fromDate:[NSDate date]].day;` — that is the day-of-month only, with no month or year.
findings.failure: A user last seen at 12:30 on 14 July, viewed on 14 August, reads "last seen at 12:30" as if they were online this morning. Any last-seen whose day-of-month happens to match today is mis-labelled; everything else collapses to "last seen a long time ago", so a yesterday-evening status also reads as "a long time ago".
findings.fix: Delete the whole body of -statusForUser:completion: and implement it as `if (completion) completion(TGUserStatusInfo(user[@"status"])[@"text"]);` — TGUserStatusInfo (TGClient.m:555) already computes today/yesterday/weekday/date correctly from full year+month+day components.

findings.what: The last-seen phrase is written three times: `TGUserStatusInfo` (TGClient.m:555), `-statusForUser:completion:` (TGClient.m:1719, a worse copy — see the previous finding), and `TGUSLastSeenText` (TGClient+UserStatus.m:35). All three produce different strings for the same input: TGClient.m:579 gives "last seen today at 12:30" while TGClient.m:1747 gives "last seen at 12:30" and TGUSLastSeenText gives "last seen today at 12:30" but with a different long-ago fallback.
findings.failure: The same user shows a different subtitle in the chat header (statusForUser:), the chat list (TGUserStatusInfo via updateUserStatus) and the profile (TGClient+UserStatus.m), and a fix applied to one is invisible in the other two.
findings.fix: Keep one implementation. Promote `TGUserStatusInfo` out of TGClient.m into TGClient+Private.h as an exported `NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(NSDictionary *status)`, make -statusForUser:completion: return `TGUserStatusInfo(...)[@"text"]`, and have TGClient+UserStatus.m's TGUSLastSeenText call it instead of re-deriving the text.

findings.what: `self.pendingRequests[extra] = [completion copy];` in `-request:completion:`. Entries are removed only in -handleUpdate: (line 167) when a reply carrying the matching `@extra` arrives. There is no timeout, no purge on authorizationStateClosed, and no purge when `-start` fails.
findings.failure: When TDLib never answers — dlopen failed so `available` is NO and drainOutbox (line 133) drops nothing but never sends, or the client was closed by logOut (line 426 sets running=NO and the receive loop exits) — the completion block is retained forever and never invoked. Any screen that shows a spinner until its completion fires (e.g. TGStorageViewController's -storageStatsWithCompletion:, TGProfileViewController's -userProfile:) spins for the life of the process, and every captured view controller stays alive with it.
findings.fix: Give -request:completion: a timeout: store `@{ @"block": [completion copy], @"deadline": @(CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() + 30) }`, and from -receiveLoop (or a 5 s main-queue timer) sweep expired entries, invoking each with `@{@"@type":@"error", @"code":@(-1), @"message":@"timeout"}`. Also flush and error out every pending request in -handleAuthState: when the state is authorizationStateClosed, and in -start when it returns NO.

findings.what: `NSString *extra = [NSString stringWithFormat:@"r%lu", (unsigned long)(++self.requestSeq)];` followed by `self.pendingRequests[extra] = [completion copy];` — both run on whatever thread called -request:, while -handleUpdate: reads and mutates the same NSMutableDictionary on the main queue (lines 165-167). Neither `requestSeq` nor `pendingRequests` is protected (the only lock in the class, `outboxLock`, guards the outbox only).
findings.failure: -request: is reachable from background queues (callers such as TGChatViewController.m:3934 and TGProfileViewController.m:2046 hop to a global queue before touching the client). Two concurrent `++self.requestSeq` on a non-atomic NSUInteger property can produce the same @extra, so one caller's completion overwrites the other's and one screen never gets its reply; concurrent -setObject:forKey: against the main thread's -removeObjectForKey: can corrupt the CFDictionary's bucket array and crash in CFBasicHashAddValue.
findings.fix: Serialise both: either wrap lines 151-152 and 165-167 in a dedicated NSLock (mirroring outboxLock), or make -request:completion: enqueue its bookkeeping with `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ...)` so the seq bump, the dictionary insert and the handleUpdate lookup all happen on the main queue.

findings.what: Nine public methods declared in TGClient.h and implemented in TGClient.m have no caller anywhere outside TGClient.m/TGClient.h: -sessionsWithCompletion: (1537), -terminateSession: (1555, TGSessionsViewController.m:503 calls the category's -terminateSession:completion: instead), -setName:last: (1559), -premiumStateWithCompletion: (1473), -chatsInFolder:completion: (1865), -userForPhone:completion: (1410), -setUser:blocked: (1437), -notificationsMutedForScope:completion: + -setScope:muted: (2004/2015), -setChat:joined: (1841), and -forumTopicsForChat:completion: (1891). Two declared ivars are also unused: `fileWaiters` is allocated at line 27 and never read or written again anywhere in the tree, and `chatsAtLastLoad` is written at line 1596 and never read.
findings.failure: No runtime failure, but roughly 150 lines of TGClient.m are unreachable, three of them (forumTopicsForChat:completion:, premiumStateWithCompletion:, chatProfile: for basic groups) are actively wrong against the current td_api.tl, and a future caller wiring them up would inherit those bugs. `fileWaiters` in particular reads as live download plumbing that does not exist.
findings.fix: Delete the ten methods and their TGClient.h declarations, and remove the `fileWaiters` and `chatsAtLastLoad` properties from TGClient+Private.h (lines 36 and 43) plus the `s.fileWaiters = ...` line at TGClient.m:27 and the write at TGClient.m:1596. Keep -terminateSession: only if TGClient+Account.m's variant is removed instead.

findings.what: `-isUserBlocked:completion:` answers `completion([full[@"block_list"] isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class]);` — any non-null BlockList counts as blocked.
findings.failure: td_api has two block lists, `blockListMain` and `blockListStories`. A user muted only from stories comes back with `block_list: {"@type":"blockListStories"}`, so the profile shows "Unblock" for someone who is not actually blocked, and tapping it sends setMessageSenderBlockList with a null list, silently un-restricting their stories instead.

findings.what: `TGMessagePreview` tests `messageVideoNote` twice: line 1640 `if ([ctype isEqualToString:@"messageVideoNote"]) return @"Video message";` and again at line 1650 with the identical body.
findings.failure: The second branch is unreachable. Harmless today, but it is exactly the kind of duplicate that makes a later edit to one copy look like it had no effect.
